$comment: The Factor's board and the three chains of spec section 19. Templates are procedural: the engine picks the berths, the goods and the figures inside the ranges here, and fills {units}, {commodity}, {toPort}, {toSystem}, {fromPort}, {pay}, {hours} and {target} in the text. Charter says who posts a template, and requiresStanding keeps the better-paid work for captains a company already deals with; a template with no charter may be offered at any berth with a Factor. Pay is basePay plus perJump and perUnit, scaled so that a hold carried on commission is worth a little more than the same hold traded, because the hold is not the captain's to sell. The chains are hand-written, name their places directly, and each ends in the two-way choice the spec fixes. Endings carry only the standing they move with their own charter: `shiftStanding` moves the other two by the rival share on its own, and a second explicit figure would double-count it and break the zero-sum property the three charters are built on.

templates.title: {units} units of {commodity} to {toPort}
templates.brief: The Factor at {fromPort} requires {units} units of {commodity} at {toPort} within {hours} hours. Kessler Carriage moves what it can in its own hulls and posts the rest. Payment on delivery, less the Factor's fee.
templates.onDone: Signed for at {toPort}. {pay} marks, less the fee, and your registry against a line that closed on time.
templates.onFailed: {toPort} closed the manifest without you. Late delivery has been noted.

templates.title: {commodity} inward from {fromPort}, {units} units
templates.brief: A consignment of {units} units of {commodity} is wanted at {toPort} in {toSystem} within {hours} hours. The lane is contested and the fee is priced accordingly. Nobody here will ask how you got there.
templates.onDone: Delivered at {toPort}. {pay} marks. The Factor did not ask about the scoring on your plating.
templates.onFailed: The consignment was wanted {hours} hours ago. {toPort} has bought elsewhere and the fee is not payable.

templates.title: Priority: {units} units of {commodity}, {hours} hours
templates.brief: The yards at {toPort} are idle for want of {units} units of {commodity}. The Thirty has costed the idle hours and would rather pay you than pay them. {hours} hours, and the figure is {pay}.
templates.onDone: Entered at {toPort} against the shortfall. {pay} marks. The count will show the hours you saved.
templates.onFailed: The yards stood idle for the full {hours} hours. The cost of that is now on a sheet with your name at the top of it.

templates.title: Long haul: {units} units of {commodity} to {toSystem}
templates.brief: Prize & Salvage wants {units} units of {commodity} at {toPort} and will not send a company hull that far out for it. {hours} hours. Out there the only law is what you are carrying.
templates.onDone: Landed at {toPort} with the load intact, which is more than the last three managed. {pay} marks.
templates.onFailed: {toPort} is still waiting. Prize & Salvage has written the load off and will remember who was carrying it.

templates.title: Claim goods out of {fromPort}
templates.brief: Underwriters' Hall has settled a claim and owns {units} units of {commodity} it has no wish to store. Carry it to {toPort} and the Hall will pay {pay} marks. There is no deadline. There is also no hurry in it for anyone but you.
templates.onDone: The Hall's agent at {toPort} has taken delivery and closed the file. {pay} marks.
templates.onFailed: The goods never reached {toPort}. The Hall has opened a second file, which is one more than it likes to open about a captain.

templates.title: {units} assessors to {toPort}
templates.brief: {units} assessors and their instruments want passage to {toPort} within {hours} hours. They will want the hold swept and they will note what is in it. {pay} marks, paid on arrival.
templates.onDone: Set down at {toPort}. {pay} marks, and a written remark about your bulkheads that you may read at your leisure.
templates.onFailed: They were due at {toPort} {hours} hours ago and have said so, in writing, twice.

templates.title: {units} crew home from {fromPort}
templates.brief: A Kessler hull was written off and its crew is still at {fromPort}, on the House's account, by the hour. Carry {units} of them to {toPort}. No deadline; the House is paying for their lodging and would like to stop.
templates.onDone: {units} set down at {toPort}, which closes the lodging account. {pay} marks.
templates.onFailed: The crew is still at {fromPort} and the House is still paying for it.

templates.title: Proxies to the count at {toPort}, {hours} hours
templates.brief: {units} subscribers' proxies must be at {toPort} before the count closes in {hours} hours. A vote is weighted by shares, and a proxy that arrives late is weighted by nothing. {pay} marks.
templates.onDone: The proxies were in the room and the count carried. {pay} marks, and the Thirty knows which hull got them there.
templates.onFailed: The count closed without them. The board has recorded the result and the reason for it.

templates.title: {units} yard hands out to {toSystem}
templates.brief: {units} hands are wanted at {toPort} and have been promised a berth out within {hours} hours. They have signed articles, which makes them cargo that complains. {pay} marks.
templates.onDone: Landed at {toPort}. The hands have gone to work and {pay} marks have gone to you.
templates.onFailed: The hands are still aboard, or still at {fromPort}, and either way nobody is working at {toPort}.

templates.title: Posted: {target}
templates.brief: The Prize Court has posted {target}, who has not come in to pay the composition and is not expected to. {pay} marks on confirmation of the write-off. The Court does not care how.
templates.onDone: {target} has been written off and the posting is discharged. {pay} marks.
templates.onFailed: {target} is still flying and the posting is still open.

templates.title: {target}, for three convoys
templates.brief: Kessler Carriage has lost three convoys on this lane, and the underwriters have begun asking the sort of question that ends in a higher premium. {target} is the reason. {pay} marks. The House would do this itself, but the House does not fire first.
templates.onDone: {target} is written off. The premium will come down and nobody at Countinghouse will say your name out loud. {pay} marks.
templates.onFailed: {target} is still on the lane and the premium has gone up again.

templates.title: {target}, against the diggings
templates.brief: {target} has taken four loads off the diggings this quarter, and the tonnage is a line in the accounts that the board has begun reading aloud. {pay} marks on the write-off. The figure was voted.
templates.onDone: {target} is written off. The tonnage line closes at the quarter and somebody at Quorum will take credit for the vote. {pay} marks.
templates.onFailed: {target} is still working the lane and the line is still being read aloud.

templates.title: {target} holds no letter
templates.brief: {target} is taking prizes without a letter, which is not competition but theft, and it makes the rest of the trade look bad. {pay} marks on the write-off. The paperwork is the whole of the offence.
templates.onDone: {target} will not be filing anything further. {pay} marks, and the prize hall at Barratry has noted the service.
templates.onFailed: {target} is still taking cargo that other people have paid for the right to take.

templates.title: See a Kessler hull out of {toSystem}
templates.brief: A loaded Kessler Carriage freighter will not leave {toSystem} without a gun alongside, and the House will not arm it any heavier. Stay with it until it is out, inside {hours} hours. {pay} marks.
templates.onDone: The freighter is away and intact. {pay} marks, and the Master's log has your registry in it.
templates.onFailed: The freighter did not get out. Underwriters' Hall will settle the claim and the House will read the file.

templates.title: A loaded hull out of {toSystem}, under escort
templates.brief: Tally Extraction has a hull loaded to the brim, and the lane out of {toSystem} has cost it two this quarter. Keep this one whole for {hours} hours and the figure is {pay}. The Thirty has done the arithmetic and you are cheaper than the loss.
templates.onDone: The hull is clear of {toSystem} with its load aboard. {pay} marks, and the quarter looks better than it did.
templates.onFailed: The hull was written off in {toSystem}. The Thirty has entered the tonnage, the claim and your name in the same column.

templates.title: A condemned prize, under tow out of {toSystem}
templates.brief: A prize has been condemned and is being towed out of {toSystem} at a speed that invites company. Everyone who lost money on it knows where it is going. {hours} hours, {pay} marks, and a share if it arrives.
templates.onDone: The prize is out and on its way to be broken up. {pay} marks out of what it fetches.
templates.onFailed: The tow was taken, or shot, and the prize hall has nothing to post against the crew's account.

templates.title: {units} units of Leaf, inward, unlisted
templates.brief: Kessler sets the spread on Leaf and would like to go on setting it. Carry {units} units to {toPort} without troubling a patrol and the Reprisal Company will pay {pay} marks, which is what the spread is worth to us. Patrols scan, and a hold full of Leaf is not something a scan misses.
templates.onDone: {units} units on the ground at {toPort} and nothing on any manifest. {pay} marks.
templates.onFailed: The Leaf is confiscated and the composition is yours. Reprisal has no record of this commission and neither should you.

templates.title: {units} units of Ordnance into {toSystem}
templates.brief: The House does not post this commission. A Factor posts it, and the House does not read the board. {units} units of Ordnance are wanted at {toPort}, inside the Home Roads, where Reprisal holds the monopoly and a scan will say so. {pay} marks, paid in a room without a clerk in it.
templates.onDone: The crates are at {toPort} and the Factor's fee has been deducted from a sum that was never written down. {pay} marks.
templates.onFailed: Confiscated, with a composition to follow. The House is sorry to read about it in the Gazette.

templates.title: {units} units of Alloy, no questions, to {toPort}
templates.brief: A bonded warehouse holds {units} units of Alloy that the Thirty would say it has no right to sell inward, and has a buyer at {toPort} who does not want the argument. {hours} hours. {pay} marks. Everything about this is legal somewhere.
templates.onDone: Delivered at {toPort}, bonded and unrecorded. {pay} marks.
templates.onFailed: The Alloy is in a patrol's hold and the composition is on your account. The warehouse has never heard of you, which was the arrangement.

chains.name: The Daughters' Audit
chains.premise: Old Mrs. Kessler is dead, and her will leaves the House to "my daughters". Seven women have filed, and until the Court reads the claims the House is run by whoever is holding its books. Factor Jan Whitlock at Countinghouse wants those books moved, one sealed case at a time, in a hull nobody at the inner berths would recognise. The House pays for discretion. It does not pay for questions.

steps.title: A sealed case to Demurrage
steps.brief: Factor Whitlock has one case for the hourly berths at Demurrage, where a clerk will sign for it and nobody keeps a list of what landed. It is one jump. The House is not paying for the distance.
steps.onDone: The clerk signed, dated it, and put the receipt in a drawer with nine hundred others. 900 marks. Whitlock asks whether your hull is free this week.
steps.onFailed: The case did not reach Demurrage. Whitlock has not asked why, which is worse than asking.

steps.title: Assessor Leung to Bottomry
steps.brief: Assessor Marit Leung of the Prize Court is going out to Mendes to read the lending house's books against the House's own, and would rather not travel in a Kessler hull while she does it. Two aboard, hers and her clerk's, ten hours. She will not discuss the audit and will not stop talking about the weighing at Tare.
steps.onDone: Set down at Bottomry. Leung paid the passage herself and remarked that the House's deposits were up over a decade in which its freight was not. 1,400 marks.
steps.onFailed: Leung is still at Hallam, late for an audit, and professionally interested in why.

steps.title: The Fairlead transfer
steps.brief: The next case goes to Lading, where Kessler freight changes hulls and one more transfer will not be noticed. Supercargo Ines Carvalho acts for three of the seven claimants and has been buying lane positions off Fairlead all week. Eight hours. Fly it as though that were a coincidence.
steps.onDone: Lading has the case. Two hulls followed you out of the lane and one of them is still out there. 1,900 marks, and Whitlock has stopped pretending this is routine.
steps.onFailed: Carvalho's claimants have the case, or the case is scattered across Fairlead. Either way, three of the seven now know what is in the books.

steps.title: The hull that waited off Fairlead
steps.brief: Nahid Bello flies the Force Majeure with no letter from anyone and a retainer from somebody who files claims. She has been holding off Fairlead for four days with her transponder cold. The House will pay 3,600 marks for the write-off, and Whitlock would like it understood that the House did not fire first.
steps.onDone: The Force Majeure is written off, and Carvalho's retainer is now an expense without a result. 3,600 marks. The Gazette will carry it as an Unlettered loss, which is what it was.
steps.onFailed: Bello is still off Fairlead, and the lane is now something the House has to route around.

steps.title: The whole set to Agio
steps.brief: Whitlock wants all three cases in one hold and valued by somebody who prices things for a living. Agio will read them in an afternoon. Twelve hours, and Whitlock has written down that he instructed you to take the long way.
steps.onDone: Agio read the set and put a figure on it in the dry voice of a house that has seen worse. For ten years the dividend has been paid out of new deposits. Nothing has been stolen and nothing is there. 2,600 marks, and a clerk at Agio who will not meet your eye.
steps.onFailed: The set is not at Agio. Whoever holds it now knows what Agio would have told you.

steps.title: Soundings, and whoever meets you
steps.brief: The set is to be weighed at Tare, which is the only part of this that is procedure. Hanne Kessler, eldest of the seven, has taken a room at Tare for the week and has not filed her claim yet. The Court's hall is on the next berth over. Ten hours, 3,200 marks, and nobody has told you which of them you are delivering to.
steps.onDone: Tare weighed the cases, found them to be cases, and handed them back. Hanne Kessler is in the waiting hall. So is Assessor Leung. Both have been expecting you since Mendes.
steps.onFailed: The set did not reach Soundings. Seven claims will be read without it, and the House will go on paying its dividend out of whatever is nearest.

endings.choice: Enter the set at the Prize Court
endings.text: Leung took the cases without comment and gave you a receipt for three items of evidence. The Court sat for eleven days. Kessler & Daughters is not wound up, because nothing in the charter says a house must be solvent to be a house, but the dividend is suspended, the deposits are frozen, and the seven claims are claims on a debt. The Court paid you a witness's fee and the costs of the three flights it could document. Countinghouse has your registry on a list at the inner berths.
endings.headline: Prize Court suspends the Kessler dividend after an audit of sealed ledgers; House deposits frozen pending seven claims.

endings.choice: Hand the set to Hanne Kessler
endings.text: She read for two hours in the waiting hall, with the Court twenty paces away, and then paid you out of an account opened that morning. Six claims were withdrawn inside a week and the seventh was bought. The dividend was paid on time, out of new deposits, as it has been for ten years. Hanne Kessler holds the House, the only copy of what the books say is in a room at Countinghouse she has the key to, and you are the other person who knows.
endings.headline: Kessler & Daughters settles six claims and buys the seventh; eldest daughter confirmed at Countinghouse, dividend paid on schedule.

chains.name: Subscriber Thirty-One
chains.premise: Subscriber Pieter Mehta died off Lindqvist with his seat on the board in his pocket. The Thirty issues bearer certificates because a bearer certificate cannot be argued with, and the argument the board is now having is that whoever holds Mehta's holds one vote in thirty and the right to sit behind a door that has never been photographed. Factor Ilse Adeyemi at Quorum wants it found. The Reprisal Company wants it too, and has been bidding.

steps.title: Notice to the yard at Ullage
steps.brief: Mehta's hull was fitted at Ullage, and the yard holds the fitting-out papers, which name his lender, which names the certificate. Carry the board's notice of a missing instrument out there and bring the file back. Eight hours. Adeyemi would like this done before the Gazette works out what is missing.
steps.onDone: Ullage handed over the file without reading it. Mehta mortgaged the hull at Respondentia and insured it nowhere. 1,100 marks.
steps.onFailed: The notice is undelivered, and Ullage has now been asked the same question by somebody from Barratry.

steps.title: An assessor out to Respondentia
steps.brief: Assessor Rohan Sarkissian reads wrecks for the Thirty and wants to be at Respondentia before the lender writes the hull off and stops caring where it is. Two aboard, twelve hours. He will ask about your reactor and he will be right about it.
steps.onDone: Respondentia gave up the hull's last reported position for the price of a lunch, because a house that lends against cargo has to know where cargo is. 1,600 marks. Sarkissian has already costed the recovery.
steps.onFailed: Sarkissian did not arrive, the lender closed the file, and a hull's last position is now something three people are guessing at.

steps.title: What is left of the bridge, to Average
steps.brief: The hull is where the lender said it would be, opened up and cold. Lift the bridge safe and whatever is bolted near it, and bring it to Average, where a general average will be declared and the loss shared out among everyone who had anything aboard. Two units, ten hours.
steps.onDone: Average opened the safe in front of four parties and a clerk. The certificate was not in it. The lock had been cut with a yard tool, and the cut was three weeks old, which is two weeks before anybody filed a notice. 2,200 marks.
steps.onFailed: The safe is still out there, which makes it salvage, which makes it Flotsam's by the end of the week.

steps.title: Bid at Flotsam, paid in Alloy
steps.brief: The lot that came off Mehta's bridge is being auctioned at Flotsam, which buys without provenance and sells without warranty. Flotsam will not take the Thirty's paper, so the bid travels as twenty units of Alloy out of Specie. Nine hours; the lot is called on the hour. Reprisal will be in the room.
steps.onDone: The Alloy carried the lot, and the lot carried everything except the certificate. Master Dag Whitlock bought that separately, for cash, two days ago, and left for Bitter End the same afternoon. 2,400 marks, and Sarkissian has stopped calling this a recovery.
steps.onFailed: The lot went to a buyer from Barratry for less than you were carrying. Whatever was in it is Reprisal's business now, and so is the seat.

steps.title: Dag Whitlock, holding one vote in thirty
steps.brief: Whitlock flies the Net of Fees, holds no letter, and is at present the single most valuable captain in the Reach, which he knows. He will not sell to the Thirty at any price the Thirty will admit to. The board has voted 4,200 marks for the write-off. A bearer certificate survives its bearer; that is the entire point of one.
steps.onDone: The Net of Fees is scattered across Bitter End, and the certificate is not in the wreckage, because Whitlock had already banked it at Jettison against a hull he was not going to live to buy. 4,200 marks. Jettison holds one vote in thirty as collateral.
steps.onFailed: Whitlock is still flying and has started quoting a price in public.

steps.title: Settle at Jettison, in rounds
steps.brief: Jettison will sell the certificate back. It takes paper from nobody and has named its price in Ordnance: twenty-four units, carried in, no registry, departure tax to be decided when you are leaving. The Thirty cannot be seen buying this. You can.
steps.onDone: Twenty-four units through the door, and a folded instrument back across the same counter, with a departure tax that was decided while you were reading it. The seat is in your hold. 3,000 marks.
steps.onFailed: The Ordnance did not arrive, and Jettison has put the certificate back on the market, where there are now two bidders and a published price.

steps.title: Carry it to Quorum
steps.brief: The board sits in ten hours, and the count is posted on the outer hull within the hour of it closing. Factor Adeyemi will meet you at the inner door. Master Kerem Sarkissian of the Reprisal Company will meet you at the outer one, and has been authorised in writing to outbid the board, which tells you what the board is prepared to pay.
steps.onDone: You are standing in the one corridor in the Reach where both doors are open and both offers are real. Adeyemi has the board's figure in a sealed note. Sarkissian is not bothering with a note. 3,600 marks for the carriage, whatever you do next.
steps.onFailed: The count closed with twenty-nine votes and a gap, and the Gazette has the number.

endings.choice: Sell the certificate to the board
endings.text: Adeyemi's note was generous in the way an institution is generous when the alternative is a question in public. The Thirty bought its own seat back, entered Subscriber Thirty-One in the roll and struck him out on the same page, and the count carried that afternoon with thirty votes, as it always has. You were paid from a fund that does not appear in the accounts under that name. Barratry had the figure within a day and has formed a view about you.
endings.headline: Thirty enters a thirty-first subscriber and strikes him from the roll the same hour; Slipway Thirty unmoved on the count.

endings.text: Sarkissian paid more, in cash, in the corridor, and had it filed at Barratry before the count closed. The Reprisal Company holds one vote in thirty and the right to sit behind the door, which it exercised in the first week by sending a Master with a prize hall's manners to a meeting about ore tonnage. The Thirty has filed four actions and expects to win all of them eventually. Quorum's outer door has been photographed.
endings.headline: Reprisal Company files a bearer certificate for a seat on the Thirty; Quorum's door photographed for the first time.

chains.name: Prize Money
chains.premise: Master Ilse van der Meer of the Fair Wear and Tear holds a letter from Barratry and a crew paid in shares of what it takes. She wants a second gun that is not on the company's books and will not want a share of the hull. The prize hall posts what each crew is owed on a running board. Hers has been frozen since the Court looked at one capture off Okonjo, and a frozen board is a crew that stops being careful.

steps.title: Alongside the Fair Wear and Tear, out of Okonjo
steps.brief: Van der Meer is taking a loaded Reprisal hull out of Okonjo and wants a gun alongside that nobody has seen before. Ten hours, 1,600 marks, and you will be told nothing you do not need. Watch how a capture is done properly; the next one you see will not be.
steps.onDone: Clear of Okonjo with the hull intact. Van der Meer pays in cash, on landing, like a company that remembers being privateers. 1,600 marks, and an invitation phrased as an instruction.
steps.onFailed: The hull did not get out of Okonjo, and van der Meer has paid for a gun that was not there.

steps.title: A capture's papers to Barratry
steps.brief: The Fair Wear and Tear took a hull off Okonjo three weeks ago, flying a free captain's registry and carrying Circuitry worth rather more than the registry suggested. Carry its papers to the prize hall at Barratry to be condemned. Eight hours. Supercargo Efe Bello will sign for them and has already spent his share.
steps.onDone: Barratry read the papers, stopped, and read them again. The registry is a forgery, and under it the hull belongs to a Kessler subsidiary. Taking a rival's hull is what the charter is for. Taking a neutral is not, and on the record it was a neutral. 1,800 marks. The hall has sent the file to Soundings itself, which Bello says is the first honest thing Barratry has ever done to him.
steps.onFailed: The papers are not at Barratry and the capture is not condemned, which means it is not a capture, which means the crew has been stealing.

steps.title: The crew's statements to Escrow
steps.brief: The Court has voided the capture pending evidence and frozen the crew's shares, which are held at Escrow now, at a fee, along with the Circuitry nobody may sell. Carry the crew's sworn statements out there and bring back what Escrow is holding in the way of paper. Twelve hours. Thirty-one people are not being paid while you do this.
steps.onDone: Escrow took the statements, charged for taking them, and released the hull's own registry pages into your hold, where they had been waiting for a party that has not come forward. The pages say the hull was Kessler's. They also carry the date Barratry entered van der Meer's letter, which is two days after the capture. 2,400 marks.
steps.onFailed: Escrow holds the shares, the Circuitry and the fee clock, and the statements are somewhere else.

steps.title: Kerem Sarkissian, on retainer
steps.brief: Somebody is paying to keep those pages out of Soundings, and Sarkissian flies the Act of God without a letter, which makes the paying deniable. He has been working Sato's Error and knows what is in your hold. 4,000 marks for the write-off, out of the crew's frozen shares, which Bello has signed for on their behalf.
steps.onDone: The Act of God is written off and the retainer goes unclaimed. Sarkissian was carrying a Kessler subsidiary's provisioning receipt, which proves nothing and says everything. 4,000 marks.
steps.onFailed: Sarkissian is still out there, still paid, and still between you and Soundings.

steps.title: Out through the cordon at Landfall
steps.brief: Four hulls under a subsidiary's registry are standing off Landfall, declining to call it a blockade, because that would be an act the charter has a word for. Van der Meer is sending her tender out through them with Bello and a copy of everything aboard. Keep it whole for eight hours. 3,400 marks, and if the tender is taken the pages in your hold become the only set.
steps.onDone: The tender is out and the cordon has lifted, on the grounds that there was never a cordon. 3,400 marks. Bello will meet you at Soundings, assuming you both reach it.
steps.onFailed: The tender was taken off Landfall with the copy aboard. What is in your hold is the only evidence now, and everybody knows it.

steps.title: Inward to Soundings, under a hold of Leaf
steps.brief: The pages have to reach the Court, and a hull running empty into the Home Roads out of the Marque is a hull that gets taken apart. So it runs full: twenty units of Leaf, which Kessler holds the monopoly on, so that a patrol which scans you finds the Leaf and stops looking. Twenty hours. 4,200 marks, and a composition if it goes wrong.
steps.onDone: Tare weighed the Leaf, took its view of it, and never asked about the folder. The Court sits in the morning. Bello is in the hall with thirty-one people's shares frozen behind him, and Assessor Marit Leung has your name on the witness list.
steps.onFailed: The Leaf is confiscated, the composition is yours, and the pages are in a Court evidence locker with nobody to speak to what they mean.

endings.choice: Swear to what the pages say
endings.text: You read both halves into the record: the hull was a Kessler subsidiary's, and Barratry entered van der Meer's letter two days after she fired. Leung set a composition on the subsidiary for the forged registry and voided the capture anyway, because a capture made without a letter is not a capture. The Circuitry went back to Kessler. The crew's shares went to the composition. Thirty-one people are owed nothing and know why. The Court paid you a witness's fee and the costs of the flights it could document, and Barratry has taken your registry off the prize hall's board.
endings.headline: Prize Court voids the Okonjo capture and sets a composition on a Kessler subsidiary's forged registry; both sides leave Soundings poorer.

endings.choice: Swear the letter was served before the capture
endings.text: You said the first half and dated the second, and the pages supported you, because pages support whoever reads them aloud. Leung took the date, wrote it down, and condemned the capture as lawful, which it now is. Kessler's subsidiary paid for the forgery it had been caught in. Thirty-one shares came off the frozen board at Barratry and were paid in full, and yours was paid with them, in cash, by a Master who did not ask what you had sworn to. The Court's record contains a date that is not true, and three people know which one.
endings.headline: Okonjo capture condemned as lawful on a witness's date; Prize & Salvage posts the Fair Wear and Tear's crew in full.
